title: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness - Pre Vocational Studies - Animal Pests and Disease Control
exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: In farm animals, an abnormal condition resulting from the excessive accumulation of gases in the rumen due to the rapid fermentation of green, lush feeds is called ________.
questions.explain: Bloat is a life-threatening nutritional disease in ruminants caused by a buildup of gas in the stomach, often triggered by eating too much fresh, lush, leguminous pasture.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Newcastle disease and Foot-and-Mouth disease are highly contagious farm animal diseases caused by ________.
questions.explain: Both Newcastle disease (in poultry) and Foot-and-Mouth disease (in cattle and pigs) are major viral diseases that spread rapidly among farm animals.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: A common skin disease of farm animals characterized by circular, scaly, and itchy hairless patches on the skin is caused by ________.
questions.explain: Ringworm is a highly contagious skin infection common in livestock. Despite its name, it is a fungal disease, not caused by a worm.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following diseases is classified as a protozoan disease in farm animals?
questions.explain: Trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness) is a devastating disease caused by protozoan parasites known as trypanosomes, typically transmitted by the tsetse fly.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Farm animals can be heavily infested internally by parasites belonging to the class of ________, examples of which are tapeworms and roundworms.
questions.explain: Tapeworms, roundworms, and flukes are internally dwelling parasitic worms (helminths) that deprive farm animals of digested nutrients and cause various internal damages.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: A farm animal disease is said to be transmitted by a 'vector' when the disease pathogen is carried and spread by ________.
options: Direct physical contact between two animals
An intermediate organism like a tsetse fly or tick
questions.explain: A vector is a living organism, often an arthropod like a tsetse fly or a tick, that transmits a disease-causing pathogen from an infected animal to a healthy one.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following insect vectors is strictly responsible for transmitting the protozoan that causes trypanosomiasis in cattle?
questions.explain: The tsetse fly is the sole vector responsible for transmitting trypanosomes (which cause Trypanosomiasis or sleeping sickness) when it bites cattle to feed on their blood.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Diseases can easily be transmitted from one animal to another through contact with infected body fluids. These fluids are generally referred to as ________.
questions.explain: Discharges include saliva, nasal mucus, urine, and faeces from an infected animal. When healthy animals come in contact with these infected fluids, they can contract the disease.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: A farmer notices that his pigs are unusually inactive and refusing to eat their feed. This symptom of disease is clinically known as ________.
questions.explain: Loss of appetite (anorexia) is a primary and very common symptom indicating that an animal is sick. It involves a severe reduction in feed intake or a complete refusal to eat.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is an economic effect of diseases on farm animals?
options: It increases their daily growth rate
It reduces farm productivity and profitability
It forces them to drink more water
It makes their meat healthier for human consumption
questions.explain: Sick animals experience retarded growth, lowered milk and egg production, and high mortality rates, which overall severely reduce the farm's productivity and the farmer's profit.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: When an animal begins to drastically lose its body mass and appear unusually thin due to severe worm infestation or illness, the condition is referred to as ________.
questions.explain: Loss of weight, or emaciation, occurs because the disease disrupts nutrient digestion or causes prolonged loss of appetite, leading to severe thinness in the animal.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The practice of keeping newly purchased or sick farm animals in a separate pen to prevent the spread of diseases to the main flock is known as ________.
questions.explain: Isolation (or quarantine) is a critical method of prevention. It involves separating sick or new animals from the healthy herd to stop the potential transmission of infectious diseases.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Injecting farm animals with vaccines to stimulate their bodies to build resistance against specific viral or bacterial diseases is called ________.
questions.explain: Immunization (or vaccination) involves administering vaccines to healthy animals to create immunity, protecting them in advance against severe specific diseases.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which method of disease control involves regular sweeping of pens, cleaning feeding troughs, and providing clean water to the animals?
questions.explain: Good sanitation is an environmental control method that involves maintaining hygiene, cleaning equipment, and disposing of waste properly to eliminate the breeding grounds of disease-causing organisms.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: What is the most appropriate and hygienic method of disease control to use when a farm animal dies from a highly infectious disease?
options: Selling the meat at a lower price
Leaving the carcass in the open field for vultures
Proper disposal by deep burial or incineration
Throwing the carcass into a nearby drinking river
questions.explain: To prevent an infectious disease from spreading further to other animals and humans, dead infected animals must be safely and properly disposed of through deep burial or burning (incineration).
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: In the context of farm animal diseases, what specific role does an external parasite like a tick play?
options: It acts as a cure for viral infections
It serves as a vector that transmits disease pathogens
It digests food in the rumen
questions.explain: Ticks, tsetse flies, and mosquitoes act as vectors; they carry disease-causing pathogens (like protozoans and bacteria) and transmit them from infected animals to healthy ones when they bite.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The treatment of sick animals by administering veterinary drugs such as antibiotics is a disease control method known as ________.
questions.explain: Medication involves giving therapeutic drugs (such as antibiotics and anthelmintics) to sick animals to treat, cure, and manage existing diseases and infections.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
